newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan April trade figures.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan April trade figures.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' and analysts' initial reactions to figures for Japan's April customs-cleared trade surplus, which the government said on Monday rose 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen.
JESPER KOLL, CHIEF ECONOMIST, JP MORGAN:

"It's basically in line with expectations but there is more to come. The basic driver is going to stay intact over the next six months. The Japanese are mean and lean exporters of products that the world wants."
"Clearly America is the fastest growing OECD economy so America is going to get the lion's share of Japan's exports."

"Most economists were looking for a sharp rise in April figures. There is an anticipation that the weaker yen is going to boost exports over the medium term, fuelling a further rise. I'd like to note, though, that we don't share this conviction that the Japanese trade surplus is poised for a sharp increase. There is a very strong seasonal factor at work here, that is the strong growth in the United States. As the U.S. economy does lose momentum later in the year and the Japanese economy continues to gain steam, this suggests that the rise in the trade surplus will be capped and we won't see the sharp gains that many people are anticipating."
"The market was looking for a rather sharp increase for the whole month. The market had discounted this sort of gain," Shipley told Reuters Financial Television.
SHUJI SHIROTA, YAMAICHI RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF SECURITIES AND ECONOMICS

"The figure was very close to our forecasts. Imports jumped in March because of the consumer rush ahead of the sales tax rise and much of the jump in April's figures can be seen as a reaction to this."

"The surplus can be expected to rise over the next few months but it is too early to judge if rises of 163.7 percent will continue -- they are likely to be much smaller. The yen has risen a bit but it will take some time before this has an effect, around two to three months."
